questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`def squares(limit):` — Creates reusable behavior; without the definition, callers cannot invoke or share this rule.
`for number in range(limit):` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`yield number * number` — This line continues the calculation or control flow; omitting it removes that step and may change later results.
`print(list(squares(4)))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`def countdown(limit):` — Creates reusable behavior; without the definition, callers cannot invoke or share this rule.
`for value in range(limit, 0, -1):` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`yield value` — This line continues the calculation or control flow; omitting it removes that step and may change later results.
`print(list(countdown(3)))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately describes “Iterators, generators, and decorators”?
options: Iterators and generators process large streams without loading everything into memory; exhausted generators must be recreated.
Generators save memory by producing one item at a time from a large file or result stream; consume them deliberately.
A comprehension transforms and filters data in one expression; a regular loop can be clearer when logic grows.
Loops automate repeated work such as checking products or totaling report rows; check stop boundaries and empty collections.
questions.answer: Generators save memory by producing one item at a time from a large file or result stream; consume them deliberately.
